title: Section 45 Explained: Why Life Insurers Cannot Reject Claims After 3 Years
summary: How the Insurance Act Section 45 protects nominees and makes life policies incontestable after 36 months.
directAnswer: Under Section 45 of the Insurance Act 1938, once a life insurance policy completes 3 consecutive years from issuance or revival, the insurer is legally barred from questioning or rejecting any death claim on ANY ground, including fraud or non-disclosure of medical facts.
body:
Under Section 45 of the Insurance Act 1938 (amended in 2015), no policy of life insurance can be called in question on any ground whatsoever, including fraud or non-disclosure of material facts, after the expiry of three continuous years from the date of issuance or revival.

### Key Protections Under Section 45:
1. **Absolute Incontestability**: Once 36 continuous months lapse, the insurer forfeits the legal right to repudiate a death claim.
2. **Shifted Burden of Proof**: During the first 3 years, the insurer bears strict legal burden to prove deliberate, material misstatement.
3. **Nominee Safeguards**: Eliminates harassment of surviving beneficiaries during claim settlement periods.

faqData.question: Can an insurer repudiate a claim after 3 years if fraud is discovered?
faqData.answer: No. Under the amended Section 45 (effective 2015), the 3-year bar is absolute. Even if intentional fraud or omission is alleged, no repudiation is legally permissible once 36 continuous months pass.

faqData.question: Does the 3-year clock reset if the policy lapses and is subsequently revived?
faqData.answer: Yes. If a policy lapses due to non-payment of premiums and is later revived, the 3-year period begins afresh from the official date of revival.

faqData.question: What happens to premiums paid if a claim is rejected within the first 3 years?
faqData.answer: If repudiated for fraud within 3 years, premiums may be forfeited; however, if rejected for misstatement without fraudulent intent, the insurer must refund the premiums collected.

title: MahaRERA Carpet Area Standard: How to Avoid Paying for Balcony & Utility Air
summary: Clear guide on statutory carpet area measurements, RERA escrow protections, and penalty interest for delayed possession.
directAnswer: Under RERA legislation, developers are legally obligated to quote and sell units strictly based on RERA Net Usable Carpet Area. Selling on super built-up area or loaded square footage is a punishable statutory violation across all Indian jurisdictions.
body:
Under RERA legislation across all Indian states, builders are legally prohibited from selling apartments on super built-up or loaded square footage. Every transaction must be calculated exclusively on usable net carpet area.

### What Counts as Usable Carpet Area:
- Net usable floor area of an apartment, excluding the area covered by external walls.
- Areas under internal partition walls are included.
- Exclusive balconies or verandahs must be priced and reported as distinct line items.

faqData.question: What is the difference between RERA Carpet Area and Super Built-Up Area?
faqData.answer: RERA Carpet Area measures actual usable internal floor space between walls. Super Built-Up includes common areas (lobbies, staircases, lifts, clubhouses) marked up by 25-45% loading.

faqData.question: Can a builder change the layout and reduce carpet area after booking?
faqData.answer: No. Under RERA Section 14, any layout alteration requires prior written consent from at least two-thirds of the allottees who booked apartments in that project.

title: Cashless Hospitalization Standards: What NABH Accreditations Mean for Your Discharge
summary: Step-by-step breakdown of cashless pre-authorization, TPA query resolution limits, and hospital repudiation appeals.
directAnswer: IRDAI Master Circular mandates that insurance TPAs must grant initial cashless pre-authorization within 60 minutes and finalize discharge clearance within 180 minutes of hospital billing submission.
body:
NABH and JCI accredited hospital networks adhere to strict turnaround protocols for insurer cashless desk coordination. Learn how patient discharge settlement times are capped under standard regulatory operating procedures.

### SLA Standards:
- Pre-authorization response within 60 minutes of submission.
- Final discharge authorization within 120 minutes of complete medical file clearance.
- Direct TPA escalation desk accessible 24/7.

faqData.question: What is the penalty if a TPA takes more than 3 hours for discharge approval?
faqData.answer: Under IRDAI's revised master guidelines, insurers face regulatory fines and are barred from holding the patient or imposing hospital room rent overstays on the policyholder for TPA processing delays.

faqData.question: Can a hospital refuse cashless treatment if they are in the GIPSA / ROHINI network?
faqData.answer: No. Network hospitals bound by standard service level agreements cannot deny cashless admission to eligible active policyholders without documented technical or exclusion grounds.
